c: Burger Bay, a quick serve restaurant open from 6 a.m. to midnight
s: Burger Bay's drive-thru times have increased by 40 seconds since the lunch menu expanded. Orders are sometimes wrong, and employees collide in the small kitchen during rushes.
The franchise owner (judge) wants you to explain how to streamline work processes, coordinate the team during busy periods, and keep service fast and accurate.
p: Coordinate work with that of team members
Explain the nature of overhead/operating costs
n: Maps the order flow and removes extra steps
Assigns stations and positions based on volume
Prepares for rush by stocking, forecasting and cross-training
Checks orders at the window and tracks accuracy
Understands that waste, overtime and slow service raise costs
q: What would you do if two employees both call out right before the lunch rush?
How would you balance speed and accuracy?

c: Wrap It Up, a fast casual wrap and salad shop
s: Wrap It Up has received several online complaints about long waits on mobile orders and about employees who ignore customers waiting at the counter.
The district manager (judge) wants you to explain how to balance in-person and online customers, how to respond to complaints, and how to build a positive service culture.
p: Describe the use of technology in customer relationship management
n: Keeps a dedicated pick-up area and gives accurate wait times
Apologizes, fixes the order and offers a gesture of goodwill
Uses the app and loyalty data to personalize service
Reminds staff at huddles that every guest matters
Recognizes employees who deliver great service
q: A customer says their mobile order has been waiting for 20 minutes. What do you do?
How do you keep morale up during a long, hectic shift?

c: Taco Loft, a six-store taco restaurant brand
s: Taco Loft wants to introduce a limited-time spicy chicken taco. The marketing director wants a plan that will increase traffic without hurting the margins of the regular menu.
The marketing director (judge) wants you to explain how to use pricing, promotion and product strategy to launch a limited-time offer.
p: Explain the nature and scope of the pricing function
Identify the impact of product life cycles on marketing decisions
n: Prices to cover food cost and labor while appealing to customers
Limited-time products create urgency and fit a short life cycle
Uses in-store signage, social media, app offers and local events
Encourages sharing and tries to create excitement
Considers costs, competitors and customers' perceived value
q: How would you decide whether the limited-time taco was a success?
What would you do if the new taco took business away from your best seller?

c: Crispy Corner, a chicken sandwich restaurant
s: A Crispy Corner customer reported an allergic reaction after eating a menu item that did not list sesame on its allergen guide. A part-time employee also complained that managers ask teenage workers to stay past legal hours.
The owner (judge) wants you to explain the legal responsibilities a restaurant has to customers and employees, and what the company should do to protect everyone and itself.
p: Describe health and safety regulations in business
Comply with the spirit and intent of laws and regulations
Identify the basic torts relating to business enterprises
n: Restaurants must label allergens, follow health codes and keep records
Child labor laws limit hours; employees have rights to breaks and fair pay
Following the spirit of the law means protecting people, not just avoiding penalties
Negligence can lead to lawsuits and fines
Corrects the schedule, updates the allergen guide and trains staff
q: What would you do immediately after a customer reports an allergic reaction?
How would you respond to a manager who says the rule does not matter if nobody complains?

s: Pizza Planet Express promotes its best crew members to trainers. The area supervisor says trainers must communicate clearly, follow procedures, keep a positive attitude and help new hires succeed.

The area supervisor (judge) is interviewing you. She wants to hear how you would train a new hire, how you would handle a coworker who ignores safety rules, and what you want to learn in the next two years.
p: Explain the need for ongoing education as a worker
n: Welcomes new hires, shows them stations and explains safety and service standards
Models rules and explains why they exist
Demonstrates, observes and gives feedback
Sets specific goals such as shift lead or assistant manager
Mentions training, certifications and cross-training
q: A new hire is struggling after two shifts. What do you do?
How would you tell a coworker they are not following safety rules?
